text: In this activity, we are going to explore data through plots using KNIME.
At the end of this activity, you are going to create your first KNIME workflow.
You are going to import a data set using daily weather data from the city of San Diego,
and you are going to explore this data using plots.
As a first step, we are going to open KNIME, as I am doing here,
here, and we are going to create a new workflow in our local space.
You can use whatever name you want, in this case I'm going to use Plot Hands On, and
I'm going to click on Create.
So my new workflow has been initiated, and I can confirm this by clicking here and noticing
my new workflow in my local space.
We will proceed to load our data.
So we are going to select the CSV Reader Note, this one.
We drag it into our space.
We click on the dialog window and then we are going to select our file.
In this case I have the file in my Big Data 4 folder, the folder that you downloaded from
Chrome GitHub and we are going to select the Daily Weather CSV file.
We execute the node and on the bottom we can see our data loaded.
We can either analyze each of the rows individually or we can click on statistics and take a look
at the descriptive statistics for each column.
The first plot that we are going to create is going to be a histogram.
So we start by scrolling down this menu to the View section and selecting the Histogram
node.
We include it into our workspace and we connect the output of the CSV reader to this node.
We open the configuration and we are going to select the air temperature at 9am as the
dimension to be analyzed.
We reduce the number of bins to 10 because this is a reasonable number to work with.
We select to show a separate bar for each type of special values, and we are going to
select proportion as the frequency that the axis shows.
We click on OK, and with our configuration ready, we proceed to execute the histogram
node.
We open the view, and this is our histogram.
We can notice that the data is normally distributed.
We can also see that most of the observations are concentrated between 61 and 74 degrees Fahrenheit,
we can see a few observations of high air temperature, and on the right we see this
bar with the missing values.
The second plot is going to be a scatter plot, so first let me drag this histogram a little
it and then select the scatter plot into the workspace. I'm going to connect it with the data
and open the configuration. For the horizontal axis, I'm going to select the air temperature
at 9 a.m. and I'm going to analyze this data with the relative humidity at the same time.
So this is everything I'm going to select. I click on OK and then I proceed to run the node.
I open the view of this scatter plot and this is the plot. We can see a very clear negative
correlation between the two variables or in other words we can say that in the days in which the
the air temperature tends to be higher, the relative humidity percentage tends to be lower.
For our third plot, we want to visualize the distribution of the maximum wind direction.
However, this information is currently represented in degrees and this is not useful for us because
we need the actual cardinal direction of this wind.
So in order to achieve this, we are going to use a special type of node and we are going
to associate each of the values with its corresponding cardinal direction following the values of
a compass.
So with our steps clear, we will proceed to search for this special node which is named
a numerical binar.
This is located in the more advanced node section right here.
We drag it into our workspace and we connect it to the data.
We open the configuration window and we select the maths wind direction at 9am.
We add five binars to represent our cardinal directions because the north needs two binars.
So we start by specifying the north from 0 to 45 degrees.
we will specify it from 315 through 360, then we specify the range for the ease between
45 and 135 degrees and so on with all of the cardinal directions.
After completing the bins for our cardinal directions, we select to append this new column
and we are going to name our column a categorical max win direction at 9am.
So I type categorical right here and now I can click on OK.
So with our categorical variable ready, we can proceed to search for the var chart,
we include it into the workspace, we connect it to the numeric binar node, and I'm going to open
the configuration to make sure that the categorical max win direction is selected as the dimension
and to select the occurrence counts as the type of data to be displayed. We select the whole
workflow and I execute it using this button, which is a different approach to execute the
workflow. I open the window and this is the distribution of the max wind direction in my
data. We can notice that very few observations have wind coming from the north and that most
of the wind comes from the south and the east. And we can also notice a few missing values in
this special bar on the right.
The final plot that we're going to create
is going to be a box plot.
So first I'm going to move these two nodes a little bit
so I can create a space
and I'm going to search again for a numeric binar node.
I will put it right here in the workflow
and connect it to the data.
And this time what we are going to do
is that we are going to create a categorical variable
to indicate whether the humidity of the day was low or not,
using the relative humidity at 9 a.m.
So the first category is going to be humidity low
and the upper bound will be 25,
indicating 25% of humidity.
The second category will obviously be humidity not low
and the lower bound will be 25.
I append this new column and I'm going to call it a low humidity day so I delete
this and I type low humidity day. We can click on OK
and with our categorical variable ready we proceed to look for a new node we're
going to type conditional boxplot and we're going to select the one that says
JavaScript. So we include it into the workflow and we connect it to the
numeric binner. We open the configuration and we make sure to have on the
category column to have selected low humidity day and on the bottom we're
going to select air pressure at 9am because what we want to compare is the average air pressure
between the days in which the humidity is low versus humidity not low. So we run this,
which naturally executed the previous node, we open it, and this is our comparison. What we can
notice is that in the days in which the humidity is low, the air pressure tends to be higher
compared to the cases in which the humidity is not low. And this is how we conclude this activity.
